canonical_statement: The study aimed to derive an initial UFH dosing equation that adjusts weight-based dosing for age and body mass index.
The study aimed to internally validate whether an age- and BMI-adjusted predictive UFH dose correlates more strongly with the eventual therapeutic dose than the empiric weight-based starting dose.
The evaluation used two phases: a derivation phase and a validation phase.
Phase I retrospectively identified patients in the electronic health record from September 1 through September 30, 2015.
Phase II prospectively identified patients in an observational manner beginning in October 2015 until a prespecified 100 patients were identified.
Therapeutic anticoagulation required two consecutive aPTT values of 60 to 80 seconds on the same UFH dose.

inclusion_criteria: Two consecutive aPTT values 60-80 seconds on the same UFH dose

canonical_statement: UFH infusions were titrated with the standard institutional nurse-driven nomogram to an aPTT target of 60 to 80 seconds.
Therapeutic dose was defined as the UFH dose in units/kg/h at which a patient had two consecutive aPTT values in the 60- to 80-second target range.

outcome.definition: UFH dose at which two consecutive aPTT values were 60-80 seconds

canonical_statement: Empiric dose was defined as the weight-based UFH dose in units/kg/h at treatment initiation.
Predictive dose was defined as the weight-based UFH dose in units/kg/h adjusted for age and BMI by the predictive equation.

concept.text: Age- and BMI-adjusted predictive UFH dose

exposures.details: Calculated dose prediction; patients were actually dosed according to standard care

canonical_statement: The major endpoint compared the correlation of empiric dose with therapeutic dose against the correlation of predictive dose with therapeutic dose in the intention-to-treat validation population.
Predictive-equation derivation used multiple linear regression with one-way ANOVA, and the major endpoint comparison used a two-tailed Fisher transformation.
The institutional review board approved the study, and informed consent was waived because of the observational design and minimal patient risk.
In phase I, 169 patients were identified and 40 met criteria for the derivation cohort.
In phase II, 362 patients were identified and 101 were included in the intention-to-treat validation cohort.
The phase II per-protocol validation cohort included 73 patients.
In phase I, 65 identified patients were not included because they did not achieve at least two consecutive therapeutic-range aPTT values on the same UFH dose.

The derived predictive equation was Dose (units/kg/h) = -0.275 × BMI (kg/m²) - 0.143 × Age (years) + 33.06.

The overall predictive regression model was statistically significant by one-way ANOVA (P = .001).

The predictive-versus-empiric correlation comparison in the phase II per-protocol analysis did not reach statistical significance (P = .057).
No significant hemorrhagic or thromboembolic complications were observed during the study.
The authors stated that the observational design demonstrates mathematical correlation rather than clinical causation.
A low proportion of patients with BMI greater than 35 kg/m² limited extrapolation to severely obese patients.
The aPTT endpoint is affected by manufacturer and individual-patient variability.
Heterogeneous cancer types and therapies among patients with active cancer may have contributed additional UFH dose variability.
The authors concluded that age- and BMI-adjusted weight-based UFH dosing improved therapeutic-dose prediction and warranted evaluation in a large prospective trial assessing clinical outcomes.
The authors suggested that future analysis could evaluate chromogenic anti-factor Xa monitoring as a comparator.
